digital-culture.title: Behind the rise of the chief productivity officer and what it means for companies and employees
digital-culture.excerpt: Some employers are replacing HR directors with chief productivity officers to better align people, tech and business outcomes.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Companies are hiring chief productivity officers to oversee the intersection of people, technology, and business results, sometimes replacing traditional HR leadership. This matters because it signals that digital workplace leaders need to prove ROI on tech spending and employee experience investments rather than just managing headcount and compliance. Here's the thing though: slapping a new title on the org chart doesn't magically fix broken processes, and if you're still using seventeen different tools to manage one workflow, your new CPO is going to have a very bad time.

digital-culture.title: AI-powered professional learning: Inside the launch of Deloitte’s Scout
digital-culture.excerpt: Anthony Stephan talks about the new tool that's part of the company's $1.4 billion investment in professional development.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Deloitte launched Scout, an AI-powered learning tool that's part of their massive $1.4 billion professional development investment. This matters because it shows how major consulting firms are betting big that AI can personalize learning at scale, something most organizations struggle with. Here's the thing though: throwing $1.4 billion at a problem doesn't guarantee your people will actually use it, so the real test is whether Scout gets adoption or just becomes another underutilized platform gathering dust in your learning ecosystem.

digital-culture.title: A Danish Couple’s Maverick African Research Finds Its Moment in RFK Jr.’s Vaccine Policy
digital-culture.excerpt: The work of Peter Aaby and Christine Stabell Benn has long been controversial. Until Robert F. Kennedy Jr. became US health policy chief, most vaccine scientists tended to ignore it. Now they can’t.
digital-culture.dwp_take: A Danish researcher couple whose work questioning standard vaccine schedules is gaining mainstream attention now that RFK Jr. has influence over US health policy. This matters to digital workplace folks because misinformation spreads faster through your employee networks than accurate health data ever will, and you'll need solid communication strategies when vaccine debates hit your company channels. Look, when fringe science gets a megaphone in Washington, your IT helpdesk becomes the front line of managing workplace tension, so maybe dust off those internal communications playbooks.

industry-news.title: Balancing AI Upskilling With Quick Execution: Tips From Tech Leaders
industry-news.excerpt: AI tools and workflows can make work faster and more efficient, but they also require employees to keep refreshing their skills to use the technology effectively.
industry-news.dwp_take: Tech leaders are basically saying you need to train people on AI tools while also expecting them to deliver results yesterday, which is the eternal corporate squeeze nobody talks about enough. Digital workplace pros need to understand that skipping training to hit deadlines creates technical debt that'll cost you way more later in frustrated users and broken workflows. The dirty secret nobody mentions is that the companies actually winning at this aren't doing anything fancy; they're just accepting that real adoption takes time and protecting space for it anyway.

industry-news.title: Operationalizing Private Cloud For The ​AI-First Future
industry-news.excerpt: For companies looking to position private cloud within this next phase of cloud evolution, let's look at how to operationalize it effectively.​​
industry-news.dwp_take: Forbes is basically saying companies need to figure out how to actually run private cloud infrastructure in a way that supports AI workloads instead of just talking about it. For digital workplace leaders, this matters because your private cloud strategy directly impacts whether your organization can actually deliver AI tools to users or just looks foolish trying. Here's the thing though: most places still can't operationalize their basic cloud setups, so let's walk before we sprint toward the AI finish line.

industry-news.title: Mozilla warns UK: Breaking VPNs will not magically fix Britain's age-check mess
industry-news.excerpt: Firefox maker says the tools are basic security infrastructure, not teenage contraband
industry-news.dwp_take: Mozilla told the UK government that banning VPNs won't solve their age verification problems for adult content sites because VPNs are fundamental security infrastructure, not just tools for sneaking around restrictions. This matters to digital workplace pros because it highlights how poorly governments understand the technology they're trying to regulate, and because any blanket restrictions on VPNs would obliterate remote work security for millions of legitimate users. If your government can't tell the difference between a security tool and contraband, you've got bigger problems than a teenager with a proxy server.

industry-news.title: Google tells database devs to lean hard on AI for PostgreSQL work
industry-news.excerpt: Cloud giant says humans remain accountable, even when code gets an assist from the machines
industry-news.dwp_take: Google is telling database developers to rely heavily on AI tools when working with PostgreSQL, while still maintaining human accountability for the results. This matters to digital workplace pros because your developers are already using these tools whether you've officially blessed them or not, so you need policies that acknowledge reality instead of pretending the AI genie goes back in the bottle. Google's "humans stay accountable" line is doing a lot of heavy lifting here, because accountability is great until someone asks whose desk the bug stops at and your AI vendor vanishes into the cloud.
